cases.supported_claim: A real fleet canary became stale after devspace main advanced; Repository Intelligence surfaced the stale base and blocked advisory automation, and the integration was recreated as fresh PR #160 before merge.
non_claims: This does not establish fleet-wide stale-base incidence.
This does not establish merge readiness or acceptance authority.
FIXED refers to the rollout subject being recreated against a fresh base, not to a new engine semantic repair.

cases.supported_claim: A source-bound controlled GitHub API reproduction showed that collecting Check Runs without Commit Statuses could produce COMPLETE / NO_TERMINAL_FAILURE while a failing Commit Status existed; PR #11 repaired that acquisition gap.
non_claims: This is controlled reproduction, not observed fleet incidence.
It does not establish how often repositories use Commit Statuses.
It does not grant merge, release, or production authority.

cases.supported_claim: Current source forensics identified that documented GitHub REST Commit Status list rows normally omit sha; PR #17 proposes exact query-subject/status-URL binding and has exact-head hosted CI plus a valid advisory RIE artifact.
non_claims: PR #17 is not merged or accepted by this corpus record.
This is source-forensics evidence, not a live foreign-head fleet incident.
The positive RIE artifact for PR #17 does not prove the proposed adapter repair correct.

cases.supported_claim: After permanent fleet rollout, devspace PR #171 produced an exact-head, COMPLETE, REVIEW_READY Repository Intelligence artifact alongside successful repository CI.
non_claims: NO_TERMINAL_FAILURE in the PR-event snapshot is not a terminal-CI verdict.
This does not grant Candidate acceptance or merge authority.
This does not establish external third-party adoption.

cases.supported_claim: Repository Intelligence self-dogfooding continued after permanent rollout: PR #17 produced a valid exact-head advisory artifact and hosted RIE workflow success.
non_claims: The artifact does not independently validate PR #17's code change.
This is not a terminal-CI or merge-readiness verdict.
This does not establish broad external adoption.
